Vocabulary.d: The fixed list of all the tokens a tokenizer knows, each with its own number (token ID). Modern vocabularies have tens of thousands to a few hundred thousand entries.

Token ID.d: The number a tokenizer assigns to each token in its vocabulary. A language model actually reads and predicts token IDs, not letters or words.

Byte-pair encoding.d: A common way to build a tokenizer: start from single characters or bytes and repeatedly merge the most frequent neighbouring pair into a new token, until the vocabulary is the desired size.

Access token.d: A secret string that proves who you are to a service, such as an API key, a GitHub personal access token or a Jira API token. Completely different from the text tokens an AI model reads. Treat it like a password.

MCP server.d: A program, on your computer or on the internet, that offers an AI app a set of tools (and sometimes resources and prompts) through the Model Context Protocol, for example a browser, Jira or GitHub.

Transport.d: How an AI app and an MCP server talk to each other: stdio for a local program the app starts itself, or HTTP for a remote service.

MCP scope.d: In Claude Code, who an MCP server is set up for: local (you, this project), project (everyone, via .mcp.json) or user (you, in all your projects).

OAuth.d: A standard way to sign in to a service through your browser and grant an app limited access without giving it your password. Many remote MCP servers use it.
